question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Single-cell lineage barcoding with drug-response tracking: Introduce heritable random DNA barcodes (e.g., CellTag or CRISPR-based lineage recorders) into a clonal population, treat with the targeted drug, and track which barcoded lineages persist. This separates pre-existing drug-tolerant clones from cells that switch state after treatment, and reveals whether survival is inherited or stochastic.
2. Time-resolved single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq of persister emergence: Profile cells at high temporal resolution from before treatment through early drug exposure and into the persister state, combining transcriptome and chromatin accessibility. Identifying the cells that diverge early and the regulatory programs they activate can reveal pre-existing transcriptional or epigenetic states that predispose survival.
3. Live-cell reporter imaging linked to fate: Use fluorescent reporters for candidate survival pathways (e.g., drug target activity, stress signaling, cell-cycle phase) and time-lapse microscopy under drug to link each cell's pre-treatment reporter state to its eventual fate. This directly tests whether a measurable pre-treatment state predicts survival.
4. Genome-wide CRISPR screens comparing survivors and non-survivors: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi/a screens under the targeted drug and compare guide enrichment in surviving cells versus a drug-naive control, with time-course sampling. Hits that alter survival frequency, especially those that act without changing baseline growth, point to the genes and pathways that mediate tolerance.
5. Quantifying non-genetic heterogeneity by perturbing cell-to-cell variability: Measure the amount of drug-target expression, drug efflux, and metabolic state across single cells in the pre-treatment population, then sort or enrich for the extremes and re-test their survival. Causal experiments that isolate high- and low-variability subpopulations show whether non-genetic variation drives the survival fraction and how quickly it reverts.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Single-cell intracellular drug-load mapping
ideas.description: Quantify how much drug each cell actually accumulates, using intrinsic fluorescence of the drug, an isotope-labeled analog, or imaging mass spectrometry, and link each cell's drug load to its survival over time. If survivors take up or retain less drug, the mechanism is pharmacokinetic rather than signaling-based, which would call for dosing or transporter interventions rather than pathway inhibitors.

ideas.title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy profiling of survivors
ideas.description: Call mtDNA variants and estimate heteroplasmy in single cells using reads from existing scATAC or scRNA-seq data (for example with mgatk), then compare survivors to non-survivors. This tests the premise that the population is genetically identical, since mtDNA is not controlled by nuclear clonality, and it can reveal inherited mitochondrial genotypes that shape drug tolerance.

ideas.title: Membrane potential sorting with ion-channel perturbation
ideas.description: Stain live cells with voltage-sensitive dyes to measure resting membrane potential, sort the hyperpolarized and depolarized fractions, and re-challenge each with the drug. Then test whether pharmacological or genetic changes to specific K+ or Cl- channels shift the survival fraction, which would show a bioelectric state that predisposes cells to tolerance.

ideas.title: Dead-neighbor conditioned signaling test
ideas.description: Encapsulate single cells or defined small numbers of cells in droplets with and without supernatant or lysate from drug-killed cells, then score survival by droplet. Fractionate the active material and identify it by mass spectrometry, which tests whether dying neighbors release factors that rescue survivors.

ideas.title: Nuclear deformability and envelope-rupture phenotyping
ideas.description: Use real-time deformability cytometry to measure nuclear stiffness in untreated cells, sort by deformability, and track drug-induced nuclear envelope rupture with a fluorescent NLS reporter. Correlate lamin A/C levels with survival to test whether nuclear mechanics, rather than signaling, gates early drug-induced damage.
